pre-ride.title: Pre-ride check
pre-ride.note: Two minutes, cold, before the engine starts. In this order because each step tells you whether the next one matters.

items.label: Tyres
items.detail: Pressure by gauge, then look at the tread and the sidewall for cuts and embedded stones.

items.label: Chain
items.detail: Slack at the tightest point of rotation, not wherever it happens to be standing.

items.label: Brakes
items.detail: Lever and pedal travel, then fluid level if the reservoir has a window.

items.label: Lights
items.detail: Head, brake, indicators. Brake light on both the lever and the pedal.

items.label: Fluids
items.detail: Oil level on level ground, plus any leak that is new since yesterday.

items.label: Fasteners
items.detail: Axle nuts, sprocket bolts, anything you or anyone else touched recently.

weather.title: Weather and terrain readiness
weather.note: Judged the night before, then again at the door. A route that is fine in the dry may be a different route entirely.

items.label: Rain window
items.detail: When it is expected to start, not just whether it will rain.

items.label: Surface
items.detail: Murram sections turn to clay quickly and stay that way after the rain stops.

items.label: River crossings
items.detail: Seasonal crossings rise fast and fall slowly. Ask locally rather than guessing.

items.label: Heat
items.detail: Midday on the equator is a fatigue problem before it is a comfort problem.

items.label: Light
items.detail: Work backwards from sunset and add an hour of margin, not ten minutes.

items.label: Altitude
items.detail: A cold, wet descent after a hot climb catches riders dressed for the start.

carry.title: Essential carry list
carry.note: The set that earns its space on almost any route. Everything else is route specific.

items.label: Tyre repair
items.detail: Plugs, tool, and a way to reinflate that does not depend on finding a compressor.

items.label: Tools
items.detail: The sizes your bike actually uses, checked against your bike, not a generic set.

items.label: Water
items.detail: More than the ride needs. Dehydration reads as poor judgement long before it reads as thirst.

items.label: First aid
items.detail: Compact, and only items you already know how to use.

items.label: Documents
items.detail: Licence, insurance, registration, plus photographs of all three stored offline.

items.label: Cash
items.detail: Small notes. Fuel, repairs and help are not always card or mobile transactions.

items.label: Light
items.detail: A torch or headlamp that is not your phone, because your phone is your map.

fuel.title: Fuel and route planning
fuel.note: Plan around the single longest gap on the route, not the average distance between stations.

items.label: Longest gap
items.detail: Identify it before you leave and make sure your range covers it with margin.

items.label: Real range
items.detail: Loaded, into wind, on a rough surface. Not the range you get commuting.

items.label: Reserve
items.detail: Know what your reserve is in kilometres, tested, not assumed.

items.label: Last certain fuel
items.detail: The last station you are confident is open and stocked, not the last one on the map.

items.label: Quality
items.detail: Buy where the turnover is high. Low turnover means water and sediment.

items.label: Spare
items.detail: Carry a litre only if you have a container made for it and a safe place to mount it.

contacts.title: Emergency contact preparation
contacts.note: Prepared before the ride, because none of it is possible to arrange afterwards.

items.label: Route shared
items.detail: One person who knows where you are going and roughly when to expect you.

items.label: Check in time
items.detail: An agreed time, and an agreed action if you miss it.

items.label: Local numbers
items.detail: Stored offline in the phone and written on paper in the bike.

items.label: Medical
items.detail: Blood group, allergies and conditions, somewhere someone will find them.

items.label: Power
items.detail: A way to charge the phone that does not depend on the bike running.

items.label: Offline map
items.detail: Downloaded for the whole route before you leave signal, including the return.

workshop-prep.title: Preparing a motorcycle for a workshop visit
workshop-prep.note: Doing these five things before you arrive shortens the job and makes the estimate more accurate.

items.label: Write the symptom
items.detail: When it happens, at what speed, hot or cold, and what changes it. Not your diagnosis.

items.label: Bring the history
items.detail: What was done last, by whom, and how long ago in kilometres.

items.label: Empty the luggage
items.detail: Anything you need that day, take with you. Anything you do not, leave at home.

items.label: Fuel
items.detail: Enough to run and road test, not a full tank, which makes some jobs harder.

items.label: Say the budget
items.detail: The number you want to be called at before work continues.

roadside.title: The first ninety seconds
roadside.note: Position and visibility come before the machine. Every time, including when the fault seems trivial.

steps.title: Get off the carriageway
steps.detail: Push the bike fully clear of the lane if it will not run. A partly clear bike is a hazard, not a stopped vehicle.

steps.title: Make yourself visible
steps.detail: High visibility on, hazards on if fitted, and a warning marker back up the road further than feels necessary.

steps.title: Stand off the road
steps.detail: Not between the bike and traffic. Uphill and behind a barrier if there is one.

steps.title: Check yourself, then the pillion
steps.detail: Adrenaline hides injury. Do this deliberately before you look at the motorcycle.

steps.title: Fix your position
steps.detail: Note where you are precisely enough to tell someone. Nearest marker, town, junction, direction of travel.

steps.title: Then diagnose
steps.detail: Only now. The machine has waited this long and will wait another minute.

recovery.title: If the ride has stopped
recovery.note: Work down this list in order. Steps one to three matter whether or not any recovery service is available to you.

steps.title: Safety first, always
steps.detail: Get clear of moving traffic, make yourself visible, and check everyone before you check the machine. If anyone is injured, contact local emergency services immediately. Frontier Moto is not an emergency service.

steps.title: Fix your location
steps.detail: Road name or number, direction of travel, the last town you passed and roughly how far back. A screenshot of your map position is worth more than a description.

steps.title: Describe the machine
steps.detail: Make, model, approximate weight, whether the rear wheel turns freely, and whether it can be rolled or must be lifted.

steps.title: Describe the fault plainly
steps.detail: What happened, at what speed, what it sounded like, and what it does now. Not what you think is broken.

steps.title: State your safety status
steps.detail: Whether you are somewhere safe, whether you have water, whether it is getting dark, and whether you are alone.

steps.title: Then request
steps.detail: With the first five ready, a request takes under a minute instead of a frustrating ten.
